body.statement: Let \(n\geq 1\), let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open, and let \(F:U\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable.  If \(DF(x_0)\) is invertible at \(x_0\in U\), then there are open neighborhoods \(U_0\) of \(x_0\) and \(W_0\) of \(F(x_0)\) such that \(F|_{U_0}:U_0\to W_0\) is one-to-one and onto and has a continuously differentiable inverse.

source.verbatim_statement: f'(a) is invertible for some a in E, and b = f(a). Then there exist open sets U and V in R^n

attestation.note: Verified 2026-09-11 by downloading the cited university-hosted Rudin PDF at https://www.nara-wu.ac.jp/math/personal/moritoh/Rudin.pdf and visually inspecting Theorem 9.24 on printed p. 221 (PDF p. 230). The excerpt is contiguous and covers the invertibility premise and local-open-neighborhood conclusion used by the node.
